narrative: The model estimated a 30% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain, but it was above the bank’s decision cut-off, so your application was denied. The most influential factor was the requested loan duration. At 9 months, it is much shorter than the approved applicants’ average of about 19 months, and this worked in your favour by lowering the assessed risk. The second most important factor was your checking-account status: a negative balance below zero is uncommon among approved applicants—only about 12.6% have it, compared with 59.2% who have no negative balance—and it pushed strongly toward bad credit. Your employment history was the third key factor. Having been employed for four to seven years is relatively stable and pushed toward good credit, but it was not enough to offset the checking-account warning and the rest of your profile. Next, ask the lender which conditions would make approval possible. Focus on clearing the overdraft and showing several months of positive account balances, provide recent statements, and consider adding a guarantor or collateral or reapplying after your checking-account position improves.
